subject: ToolingBridge / Redwood - Observability adapter integration
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@toolingbridge.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood adapter - proposal and integration spec

Hi Priyom (and Camila),

Great speaking yesterday — thanks for the quick sync. As discussed, ToolingBridge would like to ship a first-class observability adapter for Redwood that streams span/trace events from the Redwood runtime into Observy (our tracing backend). The goal is to let joint customers see token-level latency, kernel selection events, and model fallback traces alongside their app traces.

I've attached a short integration spec (TB-integration-spec-v1.pdf) and a draft SOW to cover engineering and support. High-level asks from our side:
- A small Redwood SDK hook (2-3 functions) to emit per-request trace metadata (request_id, model_variant, batch_id)
- A sample adapter repo we can PR against (no breaking changes to your runtime)
- Guidance on auth (ideally short-lived key or signed JWT) and a point of contact for security/compliance review

Proposed timeline: 6 weeks to a public alpha (adapter + docs) if we can get a tech kickoff next week and an SOW signed.

Devon (cc) is our integration PM and will help coordinate the repo and test harness.

Any immediate questions? If this looks good, can we schedule a 30-min technical kickoff early next week?

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Partnerships Lead, ToolingBridge
samira@toolingbridge.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: TB-integration-spec-v1.pdf (4 pages)
Attachment: SOW-draft-ToolingBridge.docx (draft)

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood adapter - proposal and integration spec

Samira — thanks for the spec, this aligns with what I expected. I'm copying Camila (Solutions) to lead the technical kickoff and Sergio (Partner Eng) will own the adapter implementation once we scope the API points.

Quick responses to your asks:
- SDK hook: sounds reasonable — we typically accept a 3-API surface: start_trace(metadata), attach_kv(key, value), end_trace(status). Camila can confirm exact signatures.
- Sample repo: we can create a repo under redwood-inference org and expose a feature branch for your team to PR against (we prefer code-level review vs binary integration).
- Auth: short-lived service tokens are preferable; security will want to validate token rotation cadence. We'll route you to our Security team after the kickoff.

I'll block 30 minutes on Monday 2026-05-24 09:00 PT — Camila, Sergio, Samira, Devon, and I. If that doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Also: as a commercial note, if ToolingBridge wants co-marketing and joint customer trials we can discuss a reduced first-year fee for enterprise customers. Will include that in the SOW conversation.

Best,
Priyom Das
Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Redwood adapter - proposal and integration spec

Samira / Devon,

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff in a few minutes. A few technical clarifications in advance so we use the meeting for blockers and timelines:

1) Payloads and cardinality
- We want to avoid per-token network chattiness. Recommended pattern: aggregate kernel events and emit summarized spans every N tokens (configurable). The adapter can accept either batch summaries (preferred) or an optional low-volume streaming mode for debug builds.

2) KV schema
- Suggested fields: request_id, model_name, model_variant, seq_len, batch_size, kernel_version, quantization_profile, fallback_reason (optional).

3) Auth & telemetry
- Short-lived JWK-based tokens are fine. For initial alpha we can accept a static key scoped to a test org, but we will escalate to rotated tokens for any production customers. Security will request a minimal data retention SLA if traces include PII (we prefer sampled token hashes vs raw tokens).

4) Testing harness
- If you can provide a containerized test harness that emits replayed traffic at small scale (10-100 rps), we can validate latency overhead and sampling.

I'll bring an initial adapter interface proposal to the call. Sergio — can you confirm bandwidth for a 4-week engineering sprint to ship an alpha adapter if everything is agreed?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Thanks for the kickoff — productive call. To summarize next steps from Redwood Eng:

- Security: please send the contact for your SOC/compliance reviewer and we'll kick off a short evidence exchange (config screenshots, token lifecycle).
- Commercial: Priyom, happy to review the SOW and slot engineering estimates after legal accepts the draft.

Samira — tagged you in the repo and uploaded a short demo that runs locally with a mocked Observy endpoint. When you're ready we can open a PR with the adapter and a test suite.

Cheers,
